_anchors.canvas.w: 72, and 64 was measured too small rather than guessed too small. THE BOARD IS 26 px LONG and the rider's arms go up and back on the pop: at 64 the silhouette lock reported a part pixel exposed at row 0 in 9 of 12 frames of the flip. The body spans 46 px at the tuck (23 above the hips with the arms up, 23 below with the wheels) and the outline ring needs 2 more.
_anchors.canvas.h: 72, square with the width. A rolling deck sweeps its own depth into the vertical, so the cell has to hold the worst pose rather than the rest pose.
_anchors.canvas.originX: 36, dead centre. The board is symmetric about the hips and it ROLLS about its own length, so an off-centre origin would swing the deck out of the cell mid-flip. Same reasoning as the crypt's somersault cell.
_anchors.canvas.originY: 34. The hip joint, and the centre of the board's rotation. The wheels reach 25 below it and the raised hands 23 above, which leaves 11 px of margin at the worst pose.
_anchors.tones.perMaterial: 5, the idiom the 15/08 verdict selected. THE WEAVE DOES NOT REPLACE IT: the ordered dither spends range BELOW one tone step, so it adds apparent levels without taking authored ones away. Dropping to 3 was the other half of the extreme I offered him and it is not spent here — a tone count is a thing his verdict already ruled on, and the weave is a thing it has never seen.
_anchors.frames.walk: 9, and the arithmetic is the inclusive sampling rather than a preference. A clip that plays ONCE is sampled over [0,1] INCLUSIVE, so its frame times are k/(n-1) and not k/n — five phases at the quarters need (n-1) divisible by four. At 8 frames every phase but the first and last landed between frames and `src/core/contract.ts` refused the manifest. 9 frames at 38 ms is a 342 ms ollie, shorter than the 0.64 s the jump hangs for, so the clip finishes and holds while he is still in the air.
_anchors.light.x: -0.5, upper left, as every subject except the astronaut. A dusk street is lit from a low sun behind the rider's left shoulder.
_anchors.light.y: -0.58, and it is low. A long shadow street: a low lamp puts a rim along the deck's edge, which is the surface this round has to make readable.
_anchors.light.z: -0.3, toward the viewer. More front light than the crypt, because the board's TOP and UNDERSIDE both have to be legible and a grazing lamp would lose one of them.
_anchors.light.curve: 1.15. Slightly above linear, which compresses the dark end into a rim without going as far as the SOTN 1.3 — the rider is the bright thing in this picture, unlike the skull.
_anchors.gait.swing: 0.14 turn = 50 degrees at a key of 1. A tuck folds a knee much further than a pump does, and this clip's largest key is 2.6 on the far shin — 131 degrees, which is a knee at the chest. RE-DERIVED for this clip rather than carried from the pump.
_anchors.gait.lift: 3.2 px. Deeper than the pump's 2.4: an ollie crouches before it pops, and the crouch is what makes the pop read.
_anchors.gait.depth: 6 px. Unused: every clip here is authored in the screen plane or in roll.
_anchors.gait.roll: 0. THE OLLIE IS THIS ROUND'S CONTROL and it must have no roll at all. Every rotation in it is `Bone.angle`, the screen-plane path that has always worked. If the ollie reads worse than the clips before it, the roll work damaged the old path.
_anchors.body.scale: 1. The rider stands 36 px in a 240 px world, which is the runner proportion — a player needs to read three obstacles ahead.
_anchors.texture.speckle: 0. The 15/08 verdict retired per-pixel noise: random orphans read as dirt. THIS IS NOT WHAT THE DITHER BELOW IS — same histogram, different lattice, and `src/perception/weave.ts` is the only instrument that can tell them apart.
_anchors.texture.dither: **0, and the zero is this round's measured result rather than a decision not to try.** The extreme was applied and the channel refused it. At lattice 2 the rider has 0.289 of its pixels in a single-owner cell (at lattice 4: 0.000). Turning the weave on to 0.6 moved the mean tone region from 5.5 px to 4.7 — BELOW the 5 px noise floor the 15/08 verdict is calibrated against — while periodicity went only -0.140 to -0.107, still aperiodic. So it destroyed the region structure his verdict selected and returned no order for it. That is the definition of the speckle he retired. THE CAUSE IS SCALE: a 4 px limb goes from lit to dark across four pixels, so its tone bands are already one pixel wide and a half-level threshold only shuffles them. At this size the pixel-art idiom for a body is tone PLACEMENT, and dither is for surfaces — which in this game are the road and the sky, where it runs at full amplitude on a 4x4 lattice.
_anchors.texture.lattice: 2, and 4 was measured wrong for a body rather than assumed wrong. A 4x4 weave needs a 4x4 patch of one surface: the rider scores 0.000 on that share, the skeleton 0.080, the kitten 0.068. Turning both outlines off moved it not at all; doubling the body scale moved it to 0.177 — so the cause is SCALE and not the drawn line. At lattice 2 the rider recovers 0.289 of surface. 4 belongs to a road or a sky, and this project has no character big enough for it.
_anchors.shadow.steps: 7, one more than the deepest mass on the body (the chest at 3.8, the deck at 4).
_anchors.shadow.strength: 2 ramp steps. A dusk street has one low sun and asphalt does not bounce, so a shadow is nearly as dark as the crypt's.
_anchors.fill.weight: 0.1. Some bounce off the road, less than the garden's 0.16. The declared cost of a fill is that it compresses the value range, and the deck's two faces need every bit of theirs.
_anchors.outline.material: "ink". Near black with a blue cast, because the road is cool and a warm line would separate from the scene instead of from the body.
_anchors.outline.inner: true, and `Part.weld` decides where it lands. Everything on the rider is welded; the shoes against the deck and the trucks against the deck are NOT, because a shoe on a plank and a bolted truck are places the real object comes apart (his kitten note, 16/08).
_anchors.texture.facet: 0 — the facet quantiser is OFF, so this subject renders byte-identical to every version before the knob existed. Faceting snaps the surface normal to a lattice so a smooth solid shades as flat plates; it belongs to the PS1 idiom of run 21 and to nothing authored before it.
